source_evidence: These loans generally pay higher interest rates to lenders because of the higher level of risk.
answer: A leveraged loan fund invests in loans made to borrowers with high debt levels and/or low credit ratings. These loans generally pay higher interest rates because borrowers have a greater risk of default. Funds may hold a small amount of these loans or invest heavily in them. Their higher rates could mean a higher return for fund investors, but they do not guarantee one: borrowers may fail to repay, and the loans may be difficult to sell quickly. Many leveraged loans also have variable interest rates, which rise when market interest rates rise. In short, potential benefits come with credit and liquidity risks.
